evals.prompt: Use the supplied two-slide Yonsei S3 lab-meeting template to turn my research update into a polished six-slide deck. Keep the cover, top rule, left rail, logo lockup, title geometry, Arial typography, and speaker notes. The final PPTX must remain editable.
evals.expected_output: A coherent six-slide editable PPTX that reuses the supplied cover and content frames, tells one cumulative story, and has been inspected as full-size rendered slides.
expectations: The supplied source slides establish the visual style.
The opening reuses source slide 1 and the body reuses source slide 2.
Titles and inherited objects are edited in place.
New explanatory diagrams remain editable and fit the existing body area.
The final montage is visually inspected and obvious issues are fixed.

evals.prompt: Revise this 12-slide systems lab meeting. Keep its template and factual content, but make the story easier to follow, shorten dense slides, add useful mechanism diagrams, and improve the speaker notes.
evals.expected_output: A clearer editable revision that preserves the source deck's identity, improves the narrative and visuals in the actual slides, and avoids unnecessary process documents.
expectations: The communication goal and central takeaway shape the sequence.
Each slide has one main job and an audience-facing title.
Dense copy is shortened or split instead of silently shrinking the type.
Notes are adapted to slide roles and do not pad unsupported interpretation.
Only the files needed to build, render, and deliver the deck are produced.

evals.prompt: For one slide, show how requests move through an AI serving scheduler. Use restrained motion only if it makes the state change easier to understand, and keep a static fallback.
evals.expected_output: A short serving-flow animation or a static editable diagram, chosen for explanatory value, with a poster frame when motion is used.
expectations: Motion is limited to the request, queue, scheduler, GPU, and token transition.
Colors and labels match the active deck.
A poster frame preserves the explanation when animation does not play.
No decorative background motion or unrelated animation is added.
